core.title: Make each flow router route's category equal its target user/system flow's category field
core.given: A flow router and its routes.
core.when: You author or edit a flow router or a targeted user/system flow's category, and whenever CONFIRM validates any flow router (unchanged routes included).
core.then: Every flow router route declares a category (nominal/error/alternate/exception) exactly equal to the `category` field of the target user/system flow it selects.
prefer: Copy the target user/system flow's `category` value into the route.
When a user/system flow's category changes, update every route targeting it in the same change.
If the target user/system flow lacks a `category` field, set it to the intended value first, then match the route.
avoid: Deriving the category from a digit in the train identity; that legacy digit is retired and no longer parsed.
Routes with no category or a value outside nominal/error/alternate/exception.
Treating a target user/system flow without a `category` field as an exemption.
Editing whichever side is easier just to silence the mismatch, without checking which reflects intended behaviour.
core.why: Since issue #1421, category is a validated field on the user/system flow, not an identity digit, so a route's category must agree with the field it resolves to.
evidence: The stack's validator for this rule passes in CONFIRM.
For every flow router route, route.category == target user/system flow's `category` field.
verification: Checked in the validation phase CONFIRM; enforcement is confirm-blocking: a failure blocks that phase.

Scope: every flow router artifact and every route it declares, including routes unchanged in the current operation; a route that declares no category and a route whose target user/system flow has no `category` field both fail (a missing field is no exemption).

The check is a resolved-fact agreement (coherence) check: for each route it resolves the target user/system flow and compares the route's declared category with the user/system flow's `category` field; it never derives or parses the category from the user/system flow identity.
Disposition strict, severity 4, as declared in the rule's source metadata: no exception applies, and the obligation is universal over every flow router route.

On failure the finding reports both sides of the disagreement — the route's declared category and the target user/system flow's category — with identifiers of the flow router, the route and the user/system flow, and the location of the target user/system flow artifact so both sides can be inspected.

fires: CONFIRM validation of any flow router: every route is checked, including unchanged routes that already mismatch their target user/system flow.
A flow router route that declares no category at all.
A flow router route whose target user/system flow has no `category` field (the agreement cannot hold, so the route fails).
Planner adds a route, changes its category, or retargets it to a different user/system flow.
Planner changes the `category` field of a user/system flow targeted by a flow router route.
doesNotFire: A user/system flow that no flow router route targets (no route to compare against).
Edits to artifacts that are neither flow router routes nor the `category` field of a user/system flow targeted by a flow router route.

neutralityNotes: This convention is a data-agreement rule over the plan model (flow routers, routes, user/system flows) with no stack mechanics, so the core keeps the Bun wording almost verbatim: 'flow router' and 'user/system flow' are plan-domain artifact concepts (the profile vocabulary itself models user/system flows as artifacts), not stack artifacts, and the category enum (nominal/error/alternate/exception), the CONFIRM phase and the issue #1421 history are treated as shared framework/domain vocabulary. Only the checker's identifiers (validator ref, family/template/variant, term id) and the concrete failure-evidence field list — including the rule-specific user_system_flow_path field that locates the target user/system flow, which is part of this check's finding format rather than a stack-wide location-reporting convention — are realization-specific and marked bunOnly; per-rule severity and disposition stay in core.verification per the notProfileKeys list.
